title: Time Taken to Cross the Door
statement:
`n` people, numbered `0` to `n - 1`, each pass through one shared door exactly once. Person `i` reaches the door at second `arrival[i]` (`arrival` is sorted in non-decreasing order) and wants to go in when `state[i] == 0` or go out when `state[i] == 1`. Going through takes one second, at most one person can go through in any second, and anyone who has arrived may stand and wait. The door is never left unused in a second while somebody is waiting.

When people heading in different directions are waiting in the same second, the direction that goes is decided like this:

- if nobody went through the door in the previous second, a person going out goes;
- if someone went in during the previous second, a person going in goes;
- if someone went out during the previous second, a person going out goes.

If nobody waits in the preferred direction, someone from the other direction goes instead. Among the people waiting in the chosen direction, the one with the smallest index goes first.

Return an array `answer` of length `n` where `answer[i]` is the second in which person `i` goes through the door.
constraints: arrival is sorted in non-decreasing order
notes:
## Intuition

Only two things matter in any second: who is waiting to go in, who is waiting to go out, and which way the door was used a second ago. Inside one direction people leave in index order, which is also their arrival order, so each direction is a plain first-in first-out queue. Simulate the clock, adding people to their queue as they arrive and letting one person through per second. Scanning everyone each second also works, but costs O(n) per second instead of O(1).

## Approach

1. Keep two queues (`queues[0]` for going in, `queues[1]` for going out) with `front` indexes, the clock `time`, the next person to arrive `next`, and `last`, the direction used in the previous second (start with 1, since an unused door favours going out).
2. Each round, move everyone with `arrival[next] <= time` into the queue for `state[next]`.
3. If both queues are empty, jump `time` to the next arrival and reset `last = 1`, because the second before it was unused.
4. Otherwise pick `side = last`, switching to the other side if that queue is empty. Let its front person through at `time`, set `last = side`, and advance `time` by one.

## Example 1, step by step

`arrival = [0,1,1,2,4]`, `state = [0,1,0,0,1]`. At second 0 only person 0 (in) waits and goes, so `last = 0`. At second 1 persons 1 (out) and 2 (in) wait; the door was just used to go in, so person 2 goes. At second 2 person 3 (in) has joined and goes for the same reason. At second 3 only person 1 is left and goes out, and person 4 arrives and goes out at second 4. The answer is `[0,3,1,2,4]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each person is queued and dequeued once, and idle stretches are skipped in one jump.
- Space: O(n) for the queues and `answer`.

## Pitfalls

- After an idle second the preference resets to going out; forgetting to reset `last` breaks cases like `arrival = [0,2,2]`.
- The preferred direction is only a tie-break: when its queue is empty the other side goes immediately.
- Do not tick the clock one second at a time through long gaps; jump straight to the next arrival.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `queues` | waiting people: index 0 going in, index 1 going out |
| `front` | position of the first unserved person in each queue |
| `time` | the current second |
| `next` | the next person who has not reached the door yet |
| `last` | direction used in the previous second (1 if the door was unused) |
| `side` | direction chosen for this second |
| `crossed` | how many people have gone through so far |

narration.3: Two first-in first-out queues: index 0 for people going in, index 1 for people going out.
narration.8: Before anyone has used the door, it counts as unused, which favours going out.

narration.12: Everyone who has reached the door by now joins the queue for their direction.
narration.18: Nobody is waiting at this second.

narration.20: The second before that arrival was unused, so going out has priority again.
narration.23: By default repeat the direction used in the previous second.
narration.24: Nobody wants to go in, so the door goes to someone going out.
narration.25: Nobody wants to go out, so the door goes to someone going in.
narration.26: The front of the chosen queue is the smallest waiting index in that direction.
narration.28: This person goes through during the current second.
narration.29: Remember the direction for the tie-break in the next second.
narration.33: Every person now has the second they crossed.
